questions.text_english: In the ring structure of fructose, the anomeric carbon is
questions.solution: In the furanose (5-membered ring) form of fructose, the ring closure occurs at C-2, making it the anomeric carbon. C-1 is the terminal carbon with a free –CH2OH group, C-3 through C-5 are ordinary chiral carbons, and C-6 is a terminal –CH2OH. Only C-2 bears the hydroxyl group that was originally the carbonyl carbon of the open-chain ketone, so option B is correct.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा Kf का सही व्यंजक है जो विलायक की प्रकृति पर निर्भर करता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is the correct expression of Kf which depends upon the nature of solvent?
questions.solution: The cryoscopic constant Kf is derived from the thermodynamic relation for freezing point depression. The correct expression is Kf = (R × M1 × Tf²) / (1000 × ΔfusH), where R is the gas constant, M1 is the molar mass of the solvent, Tf is the freezing point of the pure solvent (in Kelvin), and ΔfusH is the enthalpy of fusion of the solvent. Option D correctly places M1 and Tf² in the numerator and ΔfusH in the denominator, making it the correct answer.

questions.text_english: Which of the following transition metals has lowest enthalpy of atomisation?
questions.solution: Manganese (Mn) has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation among the given transition metals because it has a half-filled 3d subshell (3d5) configuration which is extra stable. This stability means fewer d-electrons participate in metallic bonding, resulting in weaker metallic bonds and therefore a lower enthalpy of atomisation compared to Cr, V, and Fe. Options A, B, and D all have higher enthalpies of atomisation due to greater d-orbital participation in bonding.

questions.text_english: Which of the following curve represents the first order reaction?

options.A: Graph of t½ vs [R]0 showing a straight line with positive slope
options.B: Graph of t½ vs [R]0 showing a horizontal straight line (constant t½)
options.C: Graph of Rate vs Concentration showing a horizontal line
options.D: Graph of Rate vs Concentration showing a curve decreasing then falling

questions.solution: For a first order reaction, the half-life t½ = 0.693/k, which is independent of the initial concentration [R]0. Therefore, a graph of t½ versus [R]0 for a first order reaction is a horizontal straight line, as shown in option B. Option A (positive slope) represents a second order reaction where t½ = 1/(k[R]0). Options C and D represent rate-concentration relationships, not half-life plots.

questions.text: ऐनिलीन सीधे नाइट्रोकरण से देता है
questions.text_english: Aniline on direct nitration yields
questions.solution: The –NH2 group in aniline is a strong ortho/para director. On direct nitration with a mixed acid (HNO3 + H2SO4), aniline gets protonated to form anilinium ion (–NH3+), which is a meta director. However, a fraction of free aniline still reacts, and the net result is predominantly ortho and para products. The experimentally observed distribution is 51% ortho, 47% para, and only 2% meta, making option A correct.

questions.text_english: Which of the following is 'not' true about enantiomers?

options.A: उनकी रासायनिक अभिक्रियाशीलता समान होती है।
options.B: उनका विशिष्ट घूर्णन समान होता है।
options.C: उनके गलनांक और क्वथनांक समान होते हैं।

options_english.A: They have the same chemical reactivity.
options_english.B: They have the same specific rotation.
options_english.C: They have the same melting or boiling point.
options_english.D: They have the same refractive index.

questions.solution: Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images. They share the same physical properties such as melting point, boiling point, refractive index, and density, and also the same chemical reactivity in achiral environments. However, they differ in the direction of rotation of plane-polarised light: one rotates it clockwise (+) and the other anticlockwise (–). Therefore, their specific rotations are equal in magnitude but opposite in sign, not the same. Option B is the statement that is NOT true.

questions.text: [Co(en)3]3+ में Co की द्वितीयक संयोजकता है
questions.text_english: The secondary valency of Co in [Co(en)3]3+ is
questions.solution: According to Werner's theory, the secondary valency (coordination number) of the central metal is the total number of ligand donor atoms bonded to it. In [Co(en)3]3+, ethylenediamine (en) is a bidentate ligand with two donor nitrogen atoms. With three en ligands, the total number of donor atoms = 3 × 2 = 6. Therefore, the secondary valency (coordination number) of Co is 6, making option D correct.

questions.text: फ़ीनॉल निम्न ताप पर CS2 में Br2 के साथ अभिक्रिया करके देता है
questions.text_english: At low temperature, phenol on reaction with Br2 in CS2 gives
questions.solution: In a non-polar solvent like CS2 at low temperature, bromine exists as molecular Br2 and acts as a weak electrophile. Under these mild conditions, only monobromination occurs at the activated ortho and para positions of phenol, giving a mixture of ortho-bromophenol and para-bromophenol. Option A (tribromophenol) is obtained when phenol reacts with bromine water at room temperature due to the high polarity of water. Therefore, option B is correct.

questions.text_english: How the conductivity varies on decreasing concentration for both weak and strong electrolytes?

options.A: यह दुर्बल अपघट्य के लिए बढ़ती है और प्रबल अपघट्य के लिए घटती है।
options.B: यह दुर्बल अपघट्य के लिए घटती है और प्रबल अपघट्य के लिए बढ़ती है।
options.C: यह दुर्बल और प्रबल दोनों अपघट्यों के लिए बढ़ती है।
options.D: यह दुर्बल और प्रबल दोनों अपघट्यों के लिए घटती है।

options_english.A: It increases for weak electrolyte and decreases for strong electrolyte.
options_english.B: It decreases for weak electrolyte and increases for strong electrolyte.
options_english.C: It increases for both weak and strong electrolytes.
options_english.D: It decreases for both weak and strong electrolytes.

questions.solution: Conductivity (κ) of an electrolyte solution depends on the number of ions per unit volume. When concentration is decreased (dilution), the number of ions per unit volume decreases for both strong and weak electrolytes. For strong electrolytes, they are fully dissociated at all concentrations, so dilution simply reduces ion density and lowers conductivity. For weak electrolytes, although degree of dissociation increases on dilution, the overall number of ions per unit volume still decreases, resulting in lower conductivity. Hence option D is correct.

questions.text: CH3 – NH2, (CH3CO)2O के साथ अभिक्रिया करके देता है
questions.text_english: CH3 – NH2 on reaction with (CH3CO)2O gives
questions.solution: When methylamine (CH3–NH2) reacts with acetic anhydride (CH3CO)2O, it undergoes nucleophilic acyl substitution. The nitrogen of CH3–NH2 attacks the carbonyl carbon of acetic anhydride, displacing the acetate anion and forming N-methylacetamide: CH3–NH–CO–CH3. This is an amide bond formation (acetylation of amine). Option A is a simple amide without an N-methyl group; option B is incorrect as it suggests an ester-amine salt. Option C is the correct product.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित वक्रों में से किसके ढाल के द्वारा किसी अभिक्रिया की सक्रियण ऊर्जा निर्धारित की जा सकती है ?
questions.text_english: The activation energy of a reaction can be determined from the slope of which of the following curves?
questions.solution: The Arrhenius equation is: ln k = ln A – (Ea/R)(1/T). This is in the form y = mx + c, where y = ln k, x = 1/T, slope m = –Ea/R, and intercept c = ln A. Therefore, plotting ln k versus 1/T gives a straight line whose slope equals –Ea/R, from which activation energy Ea can be calculated as Ea = –slope × R. Option B is therefore the correct answer.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया में 'X' को पहचानिए : CH3–CO–CH2–CO–O–CH3 → NaBH4 → 'X'
questions.text_english: Identify 'X' in the following reaction: CH3–CO–CH2–CO–O–CH3 → NaBH4 → 'X'
questions.solution: NaBH4 is a mild reducing agent that selectively reduces ketones and aldehydes to alcohols but does not reduce esters, carboxylic acids, or carbon-carbon double bonds. The starting material CH3–CO–CH2–CO–O–CH3 has a ketone group (–CO–) and an ester group (–CO–O–CH3). NaBH4 reduces only the ketone group to give a secondary alcohol, leaving the ester intact. The product is therefore CH3–CH(OH)–CH2–CO–O–CH3, which is option A.

questions.text_english: What type of deviation is shown by a mixture of chloroform and acetone from Raoult's law? Give reason. What will happen to the boiling point of the solution on mixing chloroform and acetone?

key_points: Negative deviation from Raoult's law

Reason: Chloroform and acetone form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with each other (CHCl3...O=C(CH3)2), which are stronger than the interactions in pure components, reducing vapour pressure below the ideal value
Boiling point of the solution increases above the values of pure components

questions.solution: A mixture of chloroform and acetone shows negative deviation from Raoult's law. The reason is that chloroform and acetone interact with each other through intermolecular hydrogen bonding: the H of CHCl3 forms a hydrogen bond with the oxygen of acetone (C=O). This interaction is stronger than the intermolecular forces in the individual pure liquids. As a result, the tendency of molecules to escape into vapour phase decreases, lowering the vapour pressure below the ideal (Raoult's law) value. Due to this reduced vapour pressure, the boiling point of the chloroform-acetone mixture is higher than the boiling points of both pure components.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया एक चरण में सम्पन्न होती है : 2A + B → 2C
उपरोक्त अभिक्रिया का वेग किस प्रकार परिवर्तित होगा, यदि अभिक्रिया पात्र का आयतन उसके मूल आयतन से घटाकर एक तिहाई कर दिया जाए ? इस घटे हुए आयतन के साथ अभिक्रिया कोटि में क्या कोई परिवर्तन होगा ?
questions.text_english:
Following reaction takes place in one step:
2A + B → 2C
How will the rate of above reaction change if the volume of the reaction vessel is decreased to one third of its original volume? Will there be any change in the order of reaction with the reduced volume?

key_points: Rate = k[A]²[B]; when volume is reduced to 1/3, concentrations of A and B become 3 times
New rate = k[3A]²[3B] = 27 k[A]²[B] = 27 times the original rate
Order of reaction does not change with change in volume

questions.solution: Since the reaction takes place in one step, it is an elementary reaction and its rate law is: Rate = k[A]²[B]. When the volume is decreased to one-third, the concentration of each reactant becomes three times the original. The new rate = k[3A]²[3B] = k × 9[A]² × 3[B] = 27k[A]²[B]. Therefore, the rate of reaction becomes 27 times the original rate. The order of the reaction remains unchanged at 3 (second order in A, first order in B) because order is a property of the reaction mechanism, not of concentration or volume.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों के IUPAC नाम लिखिए : (i) [Ag(NH3)2][Ag(CN)2]  (ii) K3[Fe(C2O4)3]
sub_questions.text_english: Write IUPAC names of the following coordination compounds: (i) [Ag(NH3)2][Ag(CN)2]  (ii) K3[Fe(C2O4)3]

key_points: (i) Diamminesilver(I) dicyanoargentate(I)
(ii) Potassium trioxalatoferrate(III)

sub_questions.solution: For [Ag(NH3)2][Ag(CN)2]: The cation is [Ag(NH3)2]+ where Ag has +1 oxidation state and two NH3 ligands — named diamminesilver(I). The anion is [Ag(CN)2]– where Ag has +1 oxidation state and two CN– ligands — named dicyanoargentate(I). Full name: Diamminesilver(I) dicyanoargentate(I). For K3[Fe(C2O4)3]: Three K+ ions balance the complex anion [Fe(C2O4)3]3–. Fe has +3 oxidation state; C2O4²– is oxalate (a bidentate ligand), with three oxalate ligands — trioxalato. Full IUPAC name: Potassium trioxalatoferrate(III).

sub_questions.text_english: (i) Give a chemical test to show that [Co(NH3)5SO4]Cl and [Co(NH3)5Cl]SO4 are ionisation isomers.  (ii) What is meant by the 'Chelate effect'? Give an example.

key_points: (i) Add BaCl2 solution: [Co(NH3)5SO4]Cl gives white precipitate of BaSO4 (SO4²– is outside coordination sphere); [Co(NH3)5Cl]SO4 gives white precipitate with AgNO3 (Cl– is outside coordination sphere)
(ii) Chelate effect is the extra stability gained by a metal complex when polydentate (chelating) ligands form rings with the metal; example: [Cu(en)2]²+ is more stable than [Cu(NH3)4]²+

sub_questions.solution: For part (i): Add BaCl2 solution to both complexes. [Co(NH3)5SO4]Cl contains SO4²– outside the coordination sphere, so it gives an immediate white precipitate of BaSO4. [Co(NH3)5Cl]SO4 has SO4²– inside the sphere, so no precipitate with BaCl2; however, adding AgNO3 to this complex gives a white precipitate of AgCl, confirming Cl– is free. These tests confirm they are ionisation isomers. For part (ii): The chelate effect is the phenomenon by which polydentate (chelating) ligands form more stable complexes than an equivalent number of monodentate ligands, due to favourable entropy change. For example, [Cu(en)2]²+ (with two bidentate ethylenediamine ligands) is more stable than [Cu(NH3)4]²+.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित के मध्य अंतर कीजिए : (i) रेशेदार प्रोटीन और गोलिकाकार प्रोटीन  (ii) पेप्टाइड बंध और फॉस्फोडाइएस्टर बंध
questions.text_english: Differentiate between the following: (i) Fibrous protein and Globular protein  (ii) Peptide linkage and Phosphodiester linkage

sub_questions.text: रेशेदार प्रोटीन और गोलिकाकार प्रोटीन
sub_questions.text_english: Fibrous protein and Globular protein

key_points: Fibrous proteins: polypeptide chains are long and thread-like, held by hydrogen bonds; water-insoluble; structural function; e.g. keratin, collagen
Globular proteins: polypeptide chains are folded into a spherical/compact shape; water-soluble; regulatory/functional role; e.g. haemoglobin, insulin

sub_questions.solution: Fibrous proteins have polypeptide chains arranged in long parallel strands or sheets held together by hydrogen bonds. They are generally insoluble in water and serve structural functions in the body, for example keratin (in hair and nails) and collagen (in connective tissue). Globular proteins have polypeptide chains folded into compact, roughly spherical shapes and are generally soluble in water. They carry out dynamic biological functions such as catalysis (enzymes), transport (haemoglobin), and regulation (hormones like insulin).

sub_questions.text: पेप्टाइड बंध और फॉस्फोडाइएस्टर बंध
sub_questions.text_english: Peptide linkage and Phosphodiester linkage

key_points: Peptide linkage: –CO–NH– bond formed between –COOH of one amino acid and –NH2 of another; found in proteins
Phosphodiester linkage: bond formed between phosphate group and two sugar units (3' and 5' carbons) via ester bonds; found in nucleic acids (DNA/RNA)

sub_questions.solution: A peptide linkage (–CO–NH–) is the amide bond formed by a condensation reaction between the carboxyl group (–COOH) of one amino acid and the amino group (–NH2) of another, with the loss of water. It is the backbone linkage in proteins. A phosphodiester linkage is formed when a phosphate group is esterified with the 3'–OH of one sugar and the 5'–OH of another sugar, creating a –O–P(=O)(OH)–O– bridge. This type of linkage is found in the backbone of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA).

questions.text: हैलोऐरीनें नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया के प्रति कम अभिक्रियाशील क्यों होते हैं ? दो कारण दीजिए।
questions.text_english: Why are haloarenes less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reaction? Give two reasons.

key_points: Reason 1: Due to resonance, the C–X bond in haloarenes acquires partial double bond character (lone pair of X is delocalized into the ring), making the bond shorter and stronger than in haloalkanes, so it is difficult to break
Reason 2: The electron-rich aromatic ring repels the approaching nucleophile, making nucleophilic attack difficult

questions.solution: Haloarenes are less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reactions for two main reasons. First, the lone pair of electrons on the halogen atom is in conjugation with the pi electrons of the benzene ring through resonance. This gives the C–X bond a partial double bond character, making it shorter and considerably stronger than the C–X bond in haloalkanes; this strong bond is difficult to break by a nucleophile. Second, the aromatic ring in haloarenes is electron-rich, so it repels incoming nucleophiles, making nucleophilic attack on the ring carbon bearing the halogen electronically unfavourable.

questions.text: 0.61 g बेन्ज़ोइक अम्ल (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 122 g mol⁻¹) को 5 g CS2 में घोलने पर, जिसमें यह 88% तक द्वितय बनाता है, बने विलयन का क्वथनांक ज्ञात कीजिए। CS2 का क्वथनांक और Kb क्रमशः 46.2 °C और 2.3 K kg mol⁻¹ है।
questions.text_english: Calculate the boiling point of a solution containing 0.61 g of benzoic acid (Molar mass = 122 g mol⁻¹) in 5 g of CS2 in which it dimerises to the extent of 88%. The boiling point and Kb of CS2 are 46.2 °C and 2.3 K kg mol⁻¹ respectively.

key_points: Moles of benzoic acid = 0.61/122 = 0.005 mol
Degree of dimerisation α = 0.88; i = 1 – α/2 = 1 – 0.44 = 0.56

questions.solution: Moles of benzoic acid = 0.61/122 = 0.005 mol. Since benzoic acid dimerises in CS2, two molecules associate to form one dimer: 2C6H5COOH ⇌ (C6H5COOH)2. For dimerisation with degree α = 0.88, the van't Hoff factor i = 1 – α/2 = 1 – 0.88/2 = 1 – 0.44 = 0.56. Molality m = moles of solute / mass of solvent in kg = 0.005 / 0.005 = 1 mol kg⁻¹. Elevation in boiling point ΔTb = i × Kb × m = 0.56 × 2.3 × 1 = 1.288 K. Therefore, boiling point of solution = 46.2 + 1.288 = 47.488 °C ≈ 47.49 °C.

questions.text_english: Write the reaction involved in the following: (a) Reimer-Tiemann reaction  (b) Kolbe's reaction  (c) Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole

sub_questions.text: राइमर-टीमन अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Reimer-Tiemann reaction

key_points: Phenol + CHCl3 + NaOH → Salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde)
The reaction introduces a –CHO group at the ortho position of phenol

sub_questions.solution: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol reacts with chloroform (CHCl3) in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide to give salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) as the major product. The mechanism involves the formation of dichlorocarbene (:CCl2) intermediate from CHCl3 and NaOH, which then attacks the ortho position of the phenoxide ion. On hydrolysis, an aldehyde group is obtained: C6H5OH + CHCl3 + 3NaOH → 2-HO–C6H4–CHO + 3NaCl + 2H2O.

sub_questions.text: कोल्बे अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Kolbe's reaction

key_points: Sodium phenoxide + CO2 (under pressure and heat) → Sodium salicylate → Salicylic acid on acidification

sub_questions.solution: In Kolbe's reaction, sodium phenoxide (C6H5ONa) is treated with CO2 under high pressure (4–7 atm) and high temperature (125°C). CO2 acts as an electrophile and attacks the ortho position of the phenoxide ring. On acidification of the resulting product, salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) is obtained: C6H5ONa + CO2 → C6H4(OH)(COONa); upon acidification: C6H4(OH)(COONa) + HCl → C6H4(OH)(COOH) + NaCl.

key_points: Anisole + CH3COCl / AlCl3 → para-methoxycetophenull (major) + ortho-methoxyacetophenull (minor)

sub_questions.solution: In the Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole, anisole (methoxybenzene) reacts with acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) in the presence of anhydrous AlCl3 as a Lewis acid catalyst. The –OCH3 group is an ortho/para director. The acylium ion (CH3CO+) attacks predominantly the para position due to steric reasons, giving para-methoxyacetophenull as the major product, along with a minor amount of ortho-methoxyacetophenull: C6H5OCH3 + CH3COCl → para-CH3CO–C6H4–OCH3 (major) + ortho-CH3CO–C6H4–OCH3 (minor).

questions.text_english: Give reasons for the following: (a) Carboxylic acids have higher boiling point than alcohols of comparable molecular masses. (b) Alpha (α) hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones are acidic in nature. (c) Nucleophilic addition of ammonia and its derivatives does not occur with carbonyl group in strongly acidic medium.

sub_questions.text: कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्लों के क्वथनांक समतुल्य आण्विक द्रव्यमान वाले ऐल्कोहॉलों से उच्च होते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Carboxylic acids have higher boiling point than alcohols of comparable molecular masses.

key_points: Carboxylic acids form dimers via two intermolecular hydrogen bonds between two –COOH groups
This dimerisation effectively doubles the molecular mass, requiring more energy to vaporise, hence higher boiling point than alcohols

sub_questions.solution: Carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than alcohols of comparable molecular masses because carboxylic acids exist as hydrogen-bonded dimers in both liquid and vapour states. Two molecules of carboxylic acid associate through two intermolecular O–H...O hydrogen bonds involving both the C=O and the –OH of the carboxyl group. This dimerisation effectively doubles the molecular mass and requires considerably more energy to break these bonds during vaporisation, resulting in boiling points much higher than those of alcohols of similar molecular mass, which form only one hydrogen bond per molecule.

sub_questions.text: ऐल्डिहाइडों और कीटोनों के α-हाइड्रोजन परमाणुओं की प्रकृति अम्लीय होती है।
sub_questions.text_english: Alpha (α) hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones are acidic in nature.

key_points: The α-carbon is adjacent to the C=O group; removal of the α-H gives a carbanion that is stabilised by resonance with the C=O to form a resonance-stabilised enolate ion
This stabilisation makes the α-H relatively acidic

sub_questions.solution: The α-hydrogen atoms in aldehydes and ketones are acidic because the carbanion formed upon their removal is resonance-stabilised. The α-carbon is directly bonded to the electron-withdrawing carbonyl group (C=O). When the α-H is removed by a base, the resulting negative charge on the α-carbon is delocalised by resonance with the adjacent C=O group to form a stable enolate ion. This resonance stabilisation of the conjugate base lowers the energy barrier for proton removal, making the α-H acidic.

sub_questions.text: अमोनिया और इसके व्युत्पन्नों का कार्बोनिल समूह के साथ नाभिकरागी संयोजन प्रबल अम्लीय माध्यम में नहीं होता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Nucleophilic addition of ammonia and its derivatives does not occur with carbonyl group in strongly acidic medium.

key_points: In strongly acidic medium, NH3 and its derivatives (NH2OH, hydrazines, etc.) get protonated and lose their nucleophilic character
The protonated species (NH4+, NH3OH+) cannot act as nucleophiles, so nucleophilic addition does not occur

sub_questions.solution: In strongly acidic medium, ammonia and its derivatives (such as hydroxylamine and hydrazines) are protonated to form their conjugate acids (e.g. NH3 → NH4+, H2N–OH → H3N+–OH). These protonated species have no lone pair available on nitrogen to act as a nucleophile. Since the nucleophilicity of the nitrogen is destroyed by protonation, these species cannot attack the electrophilic carbonyl carbon, and nucleophilic addition does not take place in strongly acidic conditions.

questions.text:
किसी प्रथम कोटि के तापीय विघटन अभिक्रिया के लिए निम्न आँकड़े प्राप्त हुए :
C2H5Cl(g) → C2H4(g) + HCl(g)
क्रम संख्या | समय (s) | कुल दाब (atm)
1 | 0 | 0.30
2 | 30 | 0.50
वेग स्थिरांक की गणना कीजिए। [दिया है : log 3 = 0.48]
questions.text_english:
For the first order thermal decomposition reaction, following data was obtained:
C2H5Cl(g) → C2H4(g) + HCl(g)
S. No. | Time(s) | Total Pressure (atm)
1 | 0 | 0.30
2 | 30 | 0.50
Calculate rate constant. [Given: log 3 = 0.48]

key_points: At t=0: P0 = 0.30 atm. At t=30s: Ptotal = 0.50 atm
Let pressure of C2H5Cl decrease by x. Then Ptotal = (P0 – x) + x + x = P0 + x; so 0.50 = 0.30 + x, x = 0.20 atm

questions.solution: For the reaction C2H5Cl(g) → C2H4(g) + HCl(g), let the initial pressure of C2H5Cl be P0 = 0.30 atm, and let x atm of it decompose in 30 seconds. At t = 30 s: total pressure = (P0 – x) + x + x = P0 + x = 0.50 atm, so x = 0.50 – 0.30 = 0.20 atm. The partial pressure of C2H5Cl at t = 30 s is Pt = 0.30 – 0.20 = 0.10 atm. For a first order reaction: k = (2.303/t) × log(P0/Pt) = (2.303/30) × log(0.30/0.10) = (2.303/30) × log 3 = (2.303/30) × 0.48 = 1.1054/30 = 0.03685 s⁻¹. The rate constant k ≈ 3.69 × 10⁻² s⁻¹.

questions.text: आप ग्लूकोस की विवृत संरचना में निम्नलिखित की उपस्थिति कैसे स्पष्ट करेंगे ? (a) सभी छः कार्बन परमाणु ऋजु श्रृंखला में हैं। (b) पाँच –OH समूह जो भिन्न कार्बन परमाणुओं से जुड़े हैं। (c) ऐल्डिहाइड समूह
questions.text_english: How do you explain the presence of following in open structure of glucose? (a) all the six carbon atoms are in a straight chain. (b) five –OH groups which are attached to different carbon atoms. (c) an aldehyde group.

sub_questions.text: सभी छः कार्बन परमाणु ऋजु श्रृंखला में हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: All the six carbon atoms are in a straight chain.

key_points: Glucose on oxidation with HI and red phosphorus gives n-hexane, showing all six carbons in a straight (unbranched) chain

sub_questions.solution: When glucose is heated with HI and red phosphorus, all oxygen atoms are removed and n-hexane is obtained as the product. Since n-hexane is a straight-chain hydrocarbon with six carbon atoms, this confirms that all six carbon atoms in glucose are present in a straight (unbranched) chain.

sub_questions.text: पाँच –OH समूह जो भिन्न कार्बन परमाणुओं से जुड़े हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Five –OH groups which are attached to different carbon atoms.

key_points: Glucose reacts with five molecules of acetic anhydride to give glucose pentaacetate, indicating the presence of five free –OH groups attached to five different carbon atoms

sub_questions.solution: Glucose reacts with excess acetic anhydride to form glucose pentaacetate, in which five acetyl groups have replaced five hydroxyl groups. Since each acetyl group replaces one –OH group, this confirms the presence of five –OH groups. The fact that the product is glucose pentaacetate (not a higher acetate) indicates these five –OH groups are each on different carbon atoms.

sub_questions.text: ऐल्डिहाइड समूह
sub_questions.text_english: An aldehyde group.

key_points: Glucose gives a positive Tollen's test (silver mirror) and Fehling's test (brick red precipitate), reactions characteristic of aldehydes, confirming the presence of a –CHO group

sub_questions.solution: Glucose gives a positive Tollen's test (formation of silver mirror) and a positive Fehling's test (brick-red precipitate of Cu2O), which are characteristic reactions of aldehydes. Furthermore, glucose reacts with hydroxylamine (H2N–OH) to form an oxime and with hydrogen cyanide (HCN) to form a cyanohydrin, both of which are reactions typical of the aldehyde functional group. These reactions collectively confirm the presence of a –CHO group in the open chain structure of glucose.

questions.text: C4H9Br आण्विक सूत्र वाला कोई यौगिक 'X', जलीय KOH के साथ अभिक्रिया करके एक ऐल्कोहॉल देता है। इस अभिक्रिया का वेग केवल यौगिक 'X' की सांद्रता पर निर्भर करता है। जब यौगिक 'X' के ध्रुवण घूर्णक समावयव 'Y' को जलीय KOH विलयन के साथ अभिक्रियित किया गया तो अभिक्रिया वेग यौगिक 'Y' की सांद्रता और जलीय KOH दोनों पर निर्भर पाया गया।
questions.text_english: Compound 'X' with molecular formula C4H9Br reacts with aqueous KOH to give an alcohol. The rate of this reaction depends only on the concentration of the compound 'X'. When an optically active isomer 'Y' of the compound 'X' was treated with aqueous KOH solution, the rate of reaction was found to be dependent on concentration of compound 'Y' and aqueous KOH both.

sub_questions.text: 'X' और 'Y' दोनों के संरचनात्मक सूत्र लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write down the structural formula of both 'X' and 'Y'.

key_points: X is 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (tert-butyl bromide): (CH3)3CBr — follows SN1 (rate depends only on [X])
Y is 2-bromobutane (sec-butyl bromide): CH3CH(Br)CH2CH3 — optically active, follows SN2 (rate depends on [Y] and [KOH])

sub_questions.solution: Compound X follows SN1 mechanism (rate depends only on concentration of X), which is characteristic of tertiary substrates. X has formula C4H9Br and is 2-bromo-2-methylpropane: (CH3)3CBr. Compound Y is an optically active isomer of X and follows SN2 mechanism (rate depends on both [Y] and [KOH]), indicating a secondary substrate. Y is 2-bromobutane: CH3–CHBr–CH2–CH3, which is optically active because C-2 is a chiral carbon bearing four different groups.

sub_questions.text: 'X' और 'Y' में से कौन रेसिमीकरण करेगा और क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will undergo racemisation and why?

key_points: X (tert-butyl bromide) will undergo racemisation via SN1 mechanism
SN1 forms a planar carbocation intermediate that can be attacked from both faces, giving equal amounts of both enantiomers (racemic mixture)

sub_questions.solution: Compound X (2-bromo-2-methylpropane) undergoes racemisation. Since X follows the SN1 mechanism, the first step is the formation of a planar, sp2-hybridised tertiary carbocation intermediate. The hydroxide nucleophile can attack this flat carbocation with equal probability from either face, leading to a racemic mixture of the two enantiomers of the product alcohol. Though X itself does not have a chiral centre, the product 2-methyl-2-propanol from (CH3)3CBr is achiral, so racemisation is observed in the optically active tertiary substrate cases.

sub_questions.text: 'X' और 'Y' में से कौन विन्यास के प्रतिलोमन के साथ उत्पाद बनाएगा और क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will form product with inversion of configuration and why?

key_points: Y (2-bromobutane) undergoes SN2, which proceeds with complete inversion of configuration (Walden inversion)
The nucleophile attacks from the back (backside attack) leading to 100% inversion at the chiral centre

sub_questions.solution: Compound Y (2-bromobutane) forms a product with complete inversion of configuration. This is because Y undergoes the SN2 mechanism, in which the hydroxide nucleophile attacks the chiral carbon from the back face (backside attack) in a single concerted step as the bromide ion leaves from the front. This results in Walden inversion, where the configuration at the chiral centre is completely inverted. If (R)-2-bromobutane is the starting material, the product is (S)-2-butanol, and vice versa.

sub_questions.text: साम्य स्थिरांक (Kc), E°(सेल) से तो संबंधित है, लेकिन E(सेल) से नहीं। क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is the Equilibrium Constant (Kc) related to E°cell and not to Ecell?

key_points: Kc is related to E°cell because E°cell is measured at standard conditions (1 M concentration, 298 K), the same conditions at which Kc is defined
Ecell varies with concentration (given by Nernst equation), so it cannot give a single fixed value of Kc

sub_questions.solution: The equilibrium constant Kc is related to E°cell (standard EMF) and not to Ecell because E°cell is a fixed value measured at standard conditions (all ion concentrations = 1 M, 298 K, 1 atm). The relationship is ΔG° = –nFE°cell = –RT ln Kc, which gives a single fixed value of Kc for a given reaction at a given temperature. In contrast, Ecell varies with the concentrations of species in solution (as described by the Nernst equation). Since Kc is a constant dependent only on temperature, it must be related to the standard EMF E°cell, not the non-standard Ecell.

sub_questions.text: दो धातुओं 'A' और 'B' के मानक इलेक्ट्रोड विभव क्रमशः –0.24 V और +0.80 V हैं। इनमें से कौन तनु H2SO4 से हाइड्रोजन गैस निर्मुक्त करेगी ?
sub_questions.text_english: Two metals 'A' and 'B' have standard electrode potential values of –0.24 V and +0.80 V respectively. Which of these will liberate hydrogen gas from dil. H2SO4?

key_points: Metal A (E° = –0.24 V) will liberate H2 from dil. H2SO4
A metal can displace H2 only if its standard electrode potential is less than 0 V (i.e., it is above H in the electrochemical series)

sub_questions.solution: Metal A (E° = –0.24 V) will liberate hydrogen gas from dilute H2SO4. A metal can displace H2 from an acid only if its standard electrode potential is less than the standard reduction potential of H+ (which is 0.00 V). Metal A has E° = –0.24 V < 0, so it is a stronger reducing agent than hydrogen and can oxidise itself while reducing H+ to H2. Metal B has E° = +0.80 V > 0, meaning it is a weaker reducing agent than hydrogen and cannot displace H2 from dil. H2SO4.

More advantageous than dry cell because it provides constant voltage (1.35 V) throughout its life; no gas is evolved during operation

questions.text: ऐमीनों की खनिज अम्लों से अभिक्रिया द्वारा अमोनियम लवणों का बनना इनकी क्षारकीय प्रकृति को दर्शाता है। ऐलीफैटिक ऐमीन अमोनिया की अपेक्षा प्रबल क्षारक होते हैं जबकि ऐरोमैटिक ऐमीन अमोनिया से दुर्बल क्षारक होते हैं। ऐलीफैटिक तथा ऐरोमैटिक प्राथमिक एवं द्वितीयक ऐमीन ऐसिड क्लोराइड, ऐनहाइड्राइड और ऐस्टर से नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया करते हैं। ऐरोमैटिक ऐमीन की इलेक्ट्रॉनरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रियाओं में मुख्य समस्या इनकी उच्च अभिक्रियाशीलता है। प्रतिस्थापन ऑर्थों तथा पैरा दोनों स्थानों पर हो सकता है। हिन्सबर्ग अभिकर्मक प्राथमिक, द्वितीयक एवं तृतीयक ऐमीनों की पहचान एवं विभेद के लिए प्रयोग में लाया जाता है। प्रायः ऐरिलऐमीन से प्राप्त किये जाने वाले ऐरिलडाइएज़ोनियम लवण, विभिन्न प्रकार के नाभिकरागियों द्वारा प्रतिस्थापित किए जाते हैं जिसके द्वारा ऐरिल हैलाइड, सायनाइड, फ़ीनॉल तथा ऐरीन प्राप्त करने की लाभप्रद विधि उपलब्ध होती है।
questions.text_english: The reaction of amines with mineral acids to form ammonium salts shows that these are basic in nature. Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia whereas aromatic amines are weaker bases than ammonia. Aliphatic and aromatic primary and secondary amines react with acid chlorides, anhydrides and esters by nucleophilic substitution reaction. The main problem encountered during electrophilic substitution reactions of aromatic amines is that of their high reactivity. Substitution tends to occur at ortho-and para-positions. Hinsberg reagent is used for the identification and distinction between primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Aryldiazonium salts, usually obtained from arylamines, undergo replacement of the diazonium group with a variety of nucleophiles to provide advantageous methods for producing aryl halides, cyanides, phenols and arenes.

sub_questions.text: जलीय विलयन में (CH3)3N की तुलना में CH3 – NH2 प्रबल क्षारक क्यों है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why CH3 – NH2 is a stronger base than (CH3)3N in aqueous solution?

key_points: In aqueous solution, the conjugate acid (cation) of the amine is stabilised by hydrogen bonding with water
CH3NH3+ (from CH3NH2) can form three N–H...water hydrogen bonds, while (CH3)3NH+ can form only one; better solvation of CH3NH3+ makes CH3NH2 a stronger base in water

sub_questions.solution: In aqueous solution, the basicity of an amine depends on the stability of its conjugate acid (ammonium ion) through solvation by water. The conjugate acid of methylamine, CH3NH3+, has three N–H bonds available for hydrogen bonding with water molecules, which greatly stabilises it through solvation. On the other hand, the conjugate acid of trimethylamine, (CH3)3NH+, has only one N–H bond available for hydrogen bonding with water, resulting in much weaker solvation. Therefore, CH3NH2 forms a more stable conjugate acid in water and is a stronger base than (CH3)3N in aqueous solution.

sub_questions.text: यौगिक A और B के संरचनात्मक सूत्र लिखिए : CH3CONH2 →(NaOBr)→ A →(C6H5COCl/क्षार)→ B
sub_questions.text_english: Write structural formulae of the compound A and B: CH3CONH2 →(NaOBr)→ A →(C6H5COCl/Base)→ B

key_points: A is CH3NH2 (methylamine) — formed by Hoffmann bromamide degradation of acetamide
B is CH3NH–CO–C6H5 (N-methylbenzamide) — formed by reaction of CH3NH2 with benzoyl chloride in presence of base

sub_questions.solution: Step 1: CH3CONH2 reacts with NaOBr (Hoffmann bromamide reaction) to give A = CH3NH2 (methylamine). In this reaction, the amide loses one carbon as CO2 while the nitrogen is retained, giving a primary amine with one fewer carbon. Step 2: Methylamine (CH3NH2) reacts with benzoyl chloride (C6H5COCl) in the presence of a base (which neutralises the HCl formed) to give B = CH3NH–CO–C6H5 (N-methylbenzamide). This is a nucleophilic acyl substitution where the NH2 of methylamine attacks the acyl carbon.

sub_questions.text: C3H9N आण्विक सूत्र वाला कोई यौगिक 'X' हिन्सबर्ग अभिकर्मक के साथ अभिक्रिया करके एक उत्पाद देता है जो क्षार में अविलेय है। 'X' की पहचान कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: A compound 'X' with molecular formula C3H9N reacts with Hinsberg reagent to give a product insoluble in alkali. Identify 'X'.

key_points: X is a secondary amine
Secondary amines react with Hinsberg reagent (benzenesulphonyl chloride) to give a sulphonamide that is insoluble in alkali (N-disubstituted sulphonamide has no acidic N–H)
X is N-methylethanamine (CH3NHCH2CH3) or diethylamine — most likely N,N-dimethylmethylamine... actually C3H9N secondary amine is N-methylethanamine (CH3–NH–C2H5)

sub_questions.solution: A product insoluble in alkali when treated with Hinsberg reagent (C6H5SO2Cl) indicates that X is a secondary amine. Primary amines give alkali-soluble sulphonamides (because the N–H is still present and acidic), while secondary amines give N,N-disubstituted sulphonamides that are insoluble in alkali. Among C3H9N isomers, the secondary amine is N-methylethanamine: CH3–NH–C2H5 (also written as C2H5NHCH3). This is compound X.

sub_questions.text: आप ऐनिलीन को बेन्ज़ोनाइट्राइल में कैसे रूपांतरित कर सकते हो ?
sub_questions.text_english: How can you convert aniline to benzonitrile?

key_points: Step 1: Aniline + NaNO2/HCl (0–5°C) → Benzenediazonium chloride (C6H5N2+Cl–)
Step 2: C6H5N2+Cl– + CuCN/KCN (Sandmeyer reaction) → Benzonitrile (C6H5CN)

sub_questions.solution: Aniline can be converted to benzonitrile in two steps. First, aniline is treated with NaNO2 and HCl at 0–5°C to form benzenediazonium chloride (C6H5N2+Cl–) via diazotisation. Second, the diazonium salt is treated with cuprous cyanide (CuCN) in the presence of KCN (Sandmeyer reaction). The diazonium group (N2+) is replaced by the cyanide group (–CN), giving benzonitrile (C6H5CN).

sub_questions.text: नाइट्रोकरण करने से पहले ऐनिलीन के –NH2 समूह का ऐसीटिलन क्यों किया जाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is –NH2 group of aniline acetylated before carrying out nitration?

key_points: To reduce the activating effect of –NH2 group so that polynitration is avoided
To protect the –NH2 group from oxidation by the nitrating mixture (HNO3/H2SO4)
Acetylation also gives better para/ortho selectivity

sub_questions.solution: The –NH2 group of aniline is acetylated before nitration for two important reasons. First, the free –NH2 group is a very strong activating group that makes the ring highly reactive, leading to polynitration (di- and tri-nitro products) under nitrating conditions. Acetylation converts it to the –NHCOCH3 group, which is a milder activating group, ensuring predominantly mono-nitration. Second, the concentrated nitrating mixture (HNO3 + H2SO4) would oxidise the free –NH2 group, destroying it. Acetylation protects the –NH2 group from oxidation. After nitration, the acetyl group is removed by hydrolysis to regenerate the –NH2 group.

questions.text: संयोजकता आबंध सिद्धांत (VBT) उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों के बनाने, चुंबकीय व्यवहार तथा ज्यामितीय आकृतियों का यथोचित स्पष्टीकरण करता है। क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत (CFT) उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों में विद्यमान केंद्रीय धातु परमाणु/आयन के d-कक्षकों की ऊर्जा की समानता पर विभिन्न क्रिस्टल क्षेत्रों के प्रभाव (लिगन्डों को बिंदु आवेश मानते हुए उनके द्वारा प्रदत्त प्रभाव) पर आधारित है। प्रबल क्षेत्र तथा दुर्बल क्षेत्र में d-कक्षकों के विपाटन से विभिन्न इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास प्राप्त होते हैं।
questions.text_english: The Valence Bond Theory (VBT) explains the formation, magnetic behaviour and geometry of coordination compounds. The Crystal Field Theory (CFT) of coordination compounds is based on the effect of different crystal fields (provided by the ligands taken as point charges), on the degeneracy of d-orbital energies of the central metal atom/ion. The splitting of the d-orbitals provides different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields.

sub_questions.text: अष्टफलकीय क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र में किन d-कक्षकों की ऊर्जा में वृद्धि होती है जब लिगन्ड केन्द्रीय धातु परमाणु/आयन के समीप जाता है ? अपने उत्तर के समर्थन में कारण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: In octahedral crystal field, energies of which d-orbitals will be raised when ligands approach the central metal atom/ion? Give reason in support of your answer.

key_points: The dz² and dx²–y² orbitals (eg set) are raised in energy
These orbitals point directly along the axes (x, y, z) towards the incoming ligands, so they experience maximum electrostatic repulsion, raising their energy

sub_questions.solution: In an octahedral crystal field, the energies of the dz² and dx²–y² orbitals (collectively called the eg set) are raised when the ligands approach along the x, y, and z axes. This is because these two orbitals have their electron density concentrated directly along the axes, pointing towards the incoming ligands. The electrostatic repulsion between the electron clouds of the ligands and the electrons in these orbitals is maximum, which raises their energy. The remaining three orbitals (dxy, dyz, dxz — the t2g set) point between the axes, experiencing less repulsion, so their energies are lowered relative to the average.

sub_questions.text: क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत का उपयोग करके, निम्नलिखित के केन्द्रीय धातु परमाणु/आयन के इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास लिखिए : (i) [CoF6]3–  (ii) [Co(NH3)6]3+ [परमाणु क्रमांक : Co = 27]
sub_questions.text_english: Using crystal field theory, write the electronic configuration of central metal atom/ion of the following: (i) [CoF6]3–  (ii) [Co(NH3)6]3+ [At. No.: Co = 27]

key_points: Co in both complexes is Co3+ (3d6 configuration)
[CoF6]3–: F– is a weak field ligand, so t2g³ eg³ (high spin, 4 unpaired electrons)
[Co(NH3)6]3+: NH3 is a strong field ligand, so t2g6 eg0 (low spin, 0 unpaired electrons)

sub_questions.solution: Co has atomic number 27, so Co3+ has the configuration [Ar]3d6. (i) In [CoF6]3–: F– is a weak field ligand, so the crystal field splitting energy Δo is small and pairing energy P > Δo. The 6 d-electrons fill with maximum unpaired electrons following Hund's rule: t2g³ eg³ (high spin complex with 4 unpaired electrons). (ii) In [Co(NH3)6]3+: NH3 is a strong field ligand, so Δo is large and P < Δo. All 6 electrons pair up in the lower t2g set: t2g6 eg0 (low spin complex with 0 unpaired electrons, diamagnetic).

sub_questions.text: [NiCl4]2– अनुचुंबकीय है जबकि [Ni(CO)4] प्रतिचुंबकीय है यद्यपि दोनों चतुष्फलकीय हैं। क्यों ? [परमाणु क्रमांक : Ni = 28]
sub_questions.text_english: [NiCl4]2– is paramagnetic while [Ni(CO)4] is diamagnetic though both are tetrahedral. Why? [Atomic No.: Ni = 28]

key_points: In [NiCl4]2–: Ni is +2 (3d8); Cl– is weak field ligand; 2 unpaired electrons remain → paramagnetic
In [Ni(CO)4]: Ni is 0 (3d10, sp3 hybridisation); CO is strong field; all electrons paired → diamagnetic

sub_questions.solution: Ni has atomic number 28. In [NiCl4]2–, Ni is in the +2 oxidation state with 3d8 configuration (8 d-electrons). Cl– is a weak field ligand, so in the tetrahedral field the splitting is small. With 8 d-electrons and weak splitting, 2 electrons remain unpaired, making [NiCl4]2– paramagnetic. In [Ni(CO)4], Ni is in the zero oxidation state with 3d10 configuration (10 d-electrons). CO is a very strong field ligand that causes complete pairing of all d-electrons. With all 10 d-electrons paired, [Ni(CO)4] is diamagnetic. The difference in magnetic behaviour arises from the difference in oxidation state and the field strength of the ligands.

sub_questions.text: संकुल [Fe(CN)6]3– का संकरण एवं चुंबकीय व्यवहार लिखिए। [परमाणु क्रमांक : Fe = 26]
sub_questions.text_english: Write hybridization and magnetic behaviour of the complex [Fe(CN)6]3–. [Atomic No.: Fe = 26]

key_points: Fe is +3 in [Fe(CN)6]3– with 3d5 configuration
CN– is strong field ligand: inner orbital complex, hybridisation is d2sp3
Low spin: t2g5 eg0 (1 unpaired electron), paramagnetic

sub_questions.solution: In [Fe(CN)6]3–, Fe is in the +3 oxidation state, giving a 3d5 configuration (5 d-electrons). CN– is a strong field ligand that causes large crystal field splitting, forcing the electrons into the lower t2g level. The configuration is t2g5 eg0 with one unpaired electron. According to VBT, CN– being a strong field ligand causes inner orbital complex formation: one 3d orbital is vacated (electrons pair up), and hybridisation is d2sp3 (using two 3d, one 4s, and three 4p orbitals). The complex has 1 unpaired electron and is therefore paramagnetic.

sub_questions.text: दिए गए E° मानों में E°M2+/M अनियमित प्रवृत्ति क्यों दर्शाते हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why E°M2+/M show irregular trend in the above values? [Data: V=–1.18, Cr=–0.91, Mn=–1.18, Fe=–0.44, Co=–0.28, Ni=–0.25, Cu=+0.34]

key_points: The E° values are influenced by ionisation energies, sublimation energies, and hydration enthalpies, which do not change uniformly across the period
Mn has an extra-stable half-filled 3d5 configuration so its E° is more negative; Cu has extra stability from completely filled 3d10 so its E° is positive

sub_questions.solution: The standard electrode potentials E°M²+/M show an irregular trend across the first transition series because these values are determined by three competing energy factors: ionisation energy (sum of IE1 + IE2), sublimation enthalpy, and hydration enthalpy. These three factors do not vary uniformly across the period. For example, Mn has a highly negative E° value because of the extra stability of its half-filled 3d5 configuration, which increases the ionisation energy required to form Mn²+. Cu has an exceptionally positive E° because of the extra stability of its completely filled 3d10 orbitals, reducing its tendency to ionise.

sub_questions.text: E°Cu2+/Cu मान असाधारण धनात्मक क्यों है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is E°Cu2+/Cu value exceptionally positive?

key_points: Cu has a completely filled 3d10 configuration which is extra stable
The high ionisation energy (IE1 + IE2) required to form Cu²+ is not sufficiently compensated by hydration energy, making it reluctant to form Cu²+, resulting in an exceptionally positive E°

sub_questions.solution: The E°Cu²+/Cu value is exceptionally positive (+0.34 V) because of the extra stability associated with the completely filled 3d10 electronic configuration of copper. The sum of first and second ionisation energies of Cu is relatively high due to this stability. Although hydration enthalpy of Cu²+ is significant, it is not large enough to compensate for the high ionisation energies. As a result, Cu has very little tendency to lose electrons and form Cu²+ in aqueous solution, making its electrode potential exceptionally positive.

sub_questions.text: E°Mn2+/Mn मान अत्यधिक ऋणात्मक क्यों है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why E°Mn2+/Mn value is highly negative?

key_points: Mn has a half-filled 3d5 configuration which is extra stable
High ionisation energy needed to disrupt this stable configuration, and low hydration enthalpy of Mn²+, results in a highly negative E°

sub_questions.solution: The E°Mn²+/Mn value is highly negative (–1.18 V) because manganese has an extra-stable half-filled 3d5 configuration. The first two ionisation energies of Mn are collectively high because of this extra stability, making it difficult to remove two electrons. Additionally, Mn²+ has a relatively low hydration enthalpy, so the energy released on hydration of Mn²+ does not adequately compensate for the high ionisation energies. The net result is a highly negative standard electrode potential.

sub_questions.text: पोटैशियम परमैंगनेट की अम्लीय और क्षारीय दोनों विलयनों में I⁻ के साथ ऑक्सीकरण क्रिया के लिए आयनिक समीकरणें लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the ionic equations for the oxidising action of potassium permanganate for its reaction with I⁻ in both acidic and alkaline solutions.

key_points: In acidic medium: 2MnO4⁻ + 10I⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5I2 + 8H2O
In alkaline medium: 2MnO4⁻ + I⁻ + H2O → 2MnO2 + IO3⁻ + 2OH⁻

sub_questions.solution: In acidic medium, KMnO4 is a strong oxidising agent and Mn is reduced from +7 to +2 (Mn²+). The ionic equation for its reaction with I⁻ in acidic medium is: 2MnO4⁻ + 10I⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5I2 + 8H2O. In alkaline medium, Mn is reduced from +7 to +4 (MnO2) and I⁻ is oxidised to IO3⁻. The ionic equation in alkaline medium is: 2MnO4⁻ + I⁻ + H2O → 2MnO2 + IO3⁻ + 2OH⁻.

sub_questions.text: लैन्थेनॉयड श्रेणी के सदस्य का नाम लिखिए जो (I) +4 ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था दर्शाता है और (II) +2 ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था दर्शाता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Name a member of the lanthanoid series (I) which exhibits +4 oxidation state (II) which exhibits +2 oxidation state.

key_points: (I) Cerium (Ce) exhibits +4 oxidation state (Ce4+ has stable [Xe] configuration)
(II) Europium (Eu) or Ytterbium (Yb) exhibits +2 oxidation state

sub_questions.solution: Among the lanthanoids, Cerium (Ce) is a well-known member that exhibits the +4 oxidation state. Ce4+ has a noble gas configuration [Xe] (4f0), which is extra stable, making the +4 state accessible. Europium (Eu) is a member that exhibits the +2 oxidation state. Eu2+ has the stable half-filled 4f7 configuration, which makes the +2 state relatively stable for europium. Ytterbium (Yb) also shows +2 state corresponding to the filled 4f14 configuration.

sub_questions.text: संक्रमण धातुएँ उत्तम उत्प्रेरक का कार्य क्यों करती हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why transition metals act as good catalyst?

key_points: Transition metals have variable oxidation states which allow them to form intermediate compounds with reactants
Their large surface area and ability to adsorb reactant molecules also contributes to catalytic activity

sub_questions.solution: Transition metals act as good catalysts primarily because of their ability to exhibit variable oxidation states. This allows them to form intermediate compounds with reactants, provide an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy, and then return to their original oxidation state. Additionally, transition metals and their compounds have large surface areas and the ability to adsorb reacting molecules on their surfaces (heterogeneous catalysis), which increases the effective concentration of reactants and lowers activation energy.

sub_questions.text: Mn की तुलना में Cr का गलनांक उच्च क्यों होता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why Cr has higher melting point than Mn?

key_points: Cr has configuration [Ar] 3d5 4s1, contributing 6 electrons to metallic bonding

Mn has configuration [Ar] 3d5 4s2, but the half-filled 3d5 is extra stable and less available for metallic bonding; fewer electrons effectively participate in bonding, giving weaker metallic bonds and lower melting point

sub_questions.solution: Chromium has a higher melting point than manganese because of the nature of their metallic bonding. Cr has the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d5 4s1 with six electrons available for metallic bonding. Mn has the configuration [Ar] 3d5 4s2, but its half-filled 3d5 subshell is extra stable and the electrons in it are less available for contributing to the metallic bond. As a result, the metallic bonds in Cr are stronger than in Mn, giving Cr a higher melting point (1857°C) compared to Mn (1244°C).

sub_questions.text_english: What happens when acidic solution of potassium permanganate is allowed to stand for sometime? Give the equation involved. What is this type of reaction called?

key_points: Acidic KMnO4 solution turns brown/cloudy due to formation of MnO2
4KMnO4 + 2H2SO4 → 4MnO2 + 2K2SO4 + 3O2 + 2H2O
This type of reaction is called disproportionation (auto-oxidation-reduction)

sub_questions.solution: When an acidic solution of potassium permanganate is allowed to stand for some time, the purple colour fades and a brown precipitate of MnO2 forms. This is because KMnO4 undergoes a disproportionation (auto-oxidation-reduction) reaction in acidic medium: 4KMnO4 + 2H2SO4 → 4MnO2 + 2K2SO4 + 3O2 + 2H2O. In this reaction, Mn(+7) in KMnO4 is simultaneously oxidised and reduced — some Mn atoms go to MnO2 (+4) while releasing oxygen. This type of reaction, in which the same element is both oxidised and reduced, is called a disproportionation reaction.

sub_questions.text: किसी कार्बनिक यौगिक (X) का आण्विक सूत्र C5H10O है। (X) की संरचनाएँ बनाइए यदि यह : (I) टॉलेन परीक्षण नहीं देता परन्तु धनात्मक आयडोफॉर्म परीक्षण देता है। (II) टॉलेन परीक्षण और आयडोफॉर्म परीक्षण नहीं देता, लेकिन ऐल्डॉल संघनन करता है। (III) कैनिज़ारो अभिक्रिया करता है।
sub_questions.text_english: An organic compound (X) has the molecular formula C5H10O. Draw structures for (X) if it: (I) does not give Tollen's test but gives a positive iodoform test. (II) does not give Tollen's test and iodoform test but undergoes Aldol condensation. (III) undergoes Cannizzaro's reaction.

key_points: (I) Methyl ketone: CH3–CO–CH2–CH2–CH3 (pentan-2-one) or CH3–CO–CH(CH3)2 — does not give Tollen's but gives iodoform due to CH3CO– group

(II) Aldehyde/ketone without CH3CO– and without Tollen's: CH3CH2CH2COCH3... Wait: no Tollen's means no aldehyde, no iodoform means no CH3CO–, but Aldol means α-H present → a ketone with α-H but not methyl ketone: (CH3CH2)2CO (pentan-3-one) or CH3CH2COCH2CH3
(III) Cannizzaro requires aldehyde with no α-H: (CH3)3C–CHO (2,2-dimethylpropanal, trimethylacetaldehyde)

sub_questions.solution: For a compound with formula C5H10O: Case (I) — no Tollen's test (not an aldehyde), positive iodoform (has CH3CO– group) → methyl ketone. Structure: pentan-2-one: CH3–CO–CH2–CH2–CH3. Case (II) — no Tollen's test (not an aldehyde), no iodoform (no CH3CO– group), undergoes Aldol condensation (has α-H) → a ketone with α-H but not a methyl ketone. Structure: pentan-3-one: CH3CH2–CO–CH2CH3. Case (III) — undergoes Cannizzaro's reaction, which requires an aldehyde with no α-hydrogen. Structure: 2,2-dimethylpropanal: (CH3)3C–CHO (trimethylacetaldehyde, which has no α-H due to quaternary α-carbon).

sub_questions.text_english: Show how each of the following compounds can be converted to benzoic acid: (I) Acetophenull  (II) Ethyl benzene

key_points: (I) Acetophenull (C6H5COCH3) → oxidation with alkaline KMnO4 or Cr2O7²⁻/H+ → Benzoic acid (C6H5COOH)
(II) Ethylbenzene (C6H5CH2CH3) → oxidation with alkaline KMnO4 or acidic K2Cr2O7 → Benzoic acid (C6H5COOH)

sub_questions.solution: Case (I): Acetophenull (C6H5COCH3) can be converted to benzoic acid by oxidation with alkaline KMnO4 followed by acidification. The acetyl side chain is oxidised to give a carboxylate which, on acidification, yields benzoic acid: C6H5COCH3 → [O] / KMnO4(alk.) → C6H5COOH. Case (II): Ethylbenzene (C6H5CH2CH3) can be converted to benzoic acid by vigorous oxidation with acidic or alkaline KMnO4 or K2Cr2O7/H2SO4. The entire ethyl side chain is oxidised, breaking it down to give only one –COOH group on the ring: C6H5CH2CH3 → [O] / KMnO4 → C6H5COOH.

sub_questions.text_english: Draw structure of the 2, 4-dinitrophenyl hydrazone derivative of benzaldehyde.

key_points: C6H5–CH=N–NH–C6H3(NO2)2 (2,4-dinitrophenyl group attached to nitrogen of hydrazone)
The C=N–NH– linkage connects benzaldehyde carbon to the 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine nitrogen

sub_questions.solution: The 2,4-dinitrophenyl hydrazone of benzaldehyde is formed by the reaction of benzaldehyde with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (Brady's reagent). The product is: C6H5–CH=N–NH–C6H3(NO2)2 where the carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde forms a C=N double bond with the NH2 group of 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine, and the other nitrogen is bonded to the 2,4-dinitrophenyl ring. It is an orange/yellow crystalline solid used to identify carbonyl compounds.

sub_questions.text_english: Arrange the following in increasing order of their reactivity towards HCN: Di-tert. butyl ketone, Acetaldehyde, Acetone

key_points: Reactivity towards HCN (nucleophilic addition) increases with electrophilicity of carbonyl C and decreases with steric hindrance
Increasing order: Di-tert-butyl ketone < Acetone < Acetaldehyde

sub_questions.solution: The reactivity of carbonyl compounds towards nucleophilic addition by HCN depends on the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon and the steric hindrance around it. Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones because they are less sterically hindered and the carbonyl carbon is more electrophilic. Among ketones, bulkier groups reduce reactivity. Therefore the order of increasing reactivity towards HCN is: Di-tert-butyl ketone (most hindered, least reactive) < Acetone < Acetaldehyde (least hindered, most reactive).

sub_questions.text_english: Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between benzoic acid and ethyl benzoate.

key_points: Add NaHCO3 solution: benzoic acid gives brisk effervescence (CO2) due to its acidic –COOH group; ethyl benzoate does not react with NaHCO3 and gives no effervescence

sub_questions.solution: Add sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) solution to each compound. Benzoic acid, being an acid, reacts with NaHCO3 to liberate CO2 gas with brisk effervescence: C6H5COOH + NaHCO3 → C6H5COONa + H2O + CO2↑. Ethyl benzoate is an ester and does not react with cold NaHCO3 solution, so no effervescence is observed. The compound giving brisk effervescence with NaHCO3 is benzoic acid.

sub_questions.text_english: Write the name of the reagent to convert Ethanenitrile to Ethanal.

key_points: DIBAL-H (Diisobutylaluminium hydride) at –78°C, followed by hydrolysis

sub_questions.solution: Ethanenitrile (CH3CN) can be converted to ethanal (CH3CHO) using DIBAL-H (diisobutylaluminium hydride, also called DIBAL or DIBAH) at a low temperature of –78°C. DIBAL-H partially reduces the nitrile to an imine intermediate, which on aqueous workup (hydrolysis) gives the aldehyde. The reaction is: CH3CN + DIBAL-H → [CH3CH=N–Al] → H3O+ → CH3CHO.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया में 'X' की संरचना बनाइए : cyclohexanol –(CrO3)→ 'X'
sub_questions.text_english: Draw the structure of 'X' in the following reaction: cyclohexanol –(CrO3)→ 'X'

key_points: X is cyclohexanull — CrO3 oxidises secondary alcohol to ketone

sub_questions.solution: Cyclohexanol is a secondary alcohol. When oxidised with CrO3 (chromium trioxide), secondary alcohols are converted to ketones. Therefore, cyclohexanol is oxidised to cyclohexanull: the –OH group on the ring carbon is oxidised to a C=O group. X is cyclohexanull, a six-membered ring with a ketone (carbonyl) group at position 1.
